title: System
summary: Debian's own base a minimal image can lack: kernel defaults, the clock tool, the firewall, security updates, small network checks, any USB stick's filesystem and the manual pages. Kept installed; the alternative network and time tools cached beside it.
consent: These are Debian's own packages, the ones a full Debian install has and a minimal board image leaves out. Installing them changes the box in two ways you should know about: unattended-upgrades turns on Debian's daily security updates, installed by themselves whenever the box has internet (needrestart then lists what still runs old code); and the kernel defaults switch on Debian's link protections and the rest of its settings at the next boot. The kit is kept installed: it is never removed after a while, as the others are.
notes: Each package only where it fits: Debian's kernel defaults only where the image lacks them (newer Armbian board packages ship their own), pciutils only with PCI, smartmontools only with a disk that reports SMART, AppArmor only on a kernel with it, dmidecode only on 64-bit boards.

The alternatives (ifupdown, dhcpcd-base, systemd-timesyncd) are cached, never installed with the kit: on an offline box they can't be fetched once the image's own network or time manager has failed, so they wait here for the owner's choice.
USB sticks: exFAT and NTFS as well as FAT and ISO 9660, through exfatprogs and ntfs-3g.
wtmpdb keeps the login and boot record (last, last reboot), which trixie moved out of util-linux.
